title: iTutorGroup automated age screening
system_purpose: Filter applications for remote tutoring roles
decision_impact: Automatic rejection prevented applicants from receiving recruiter consideration
verified_facts: EEOC alleged that configured software automatically rejected women aged 55 or older and men aged 60 or older.
reported_harm: Loss of employment opportunity and alleged age and sex discrimination
quantitative_evidence: EEOC reported more than 200 qualified applicants rejected and settlement relief of $365000.
limitations: The matter ended in settlement and the sources do not provide a technical audit; testimony cautions the mechanism may have been rule-based automation rather than AI.

title: Amazon experimental recruiting model
system_purpose: Rank resumes to support recruiter prioritization
decision_impact: Lower ranking could reduce recruiter attention for qualified applicants
verified_facts: EEOC-hosted testimony recounts reports that Amazon developed the tool from 2014 and abandoned it after observing disadvantage to women.
reported_harm: Foreseeable discriminatory opportunity loss caused by gender-correlated historical patterns
quantitative_evidence: The source reports development dates but provides no affected-applicant count denominator or deployed decision rate.
limitations: This was a reported experimental system rather than a regulator finding about a production deployment; causal and performance details are incomplete.

title: Algorithmic screening and disability accommodation risk
system_purpose: Assess or score job applicants with automated tools
decision_impact: Assessment design may screen out applicants who could perform the job with accommodation
verified_facts: EEOC and DOJ issued technical assistance stating that software and AI employment tools can disadvantage people with disabilities without safeguards.
reported_harm: Foreseeable exclusion from employment when accommodation or an alternative assessment is unavailable
quantitative_evidence: The guidance identifies three primary ADA concern areas but does not estimate a universal incident rate.
limitations: This is authoritative risk guidance rather than one named employer incident and United States legal rules are not directly transferable to the target market.
